he.layout.error: Could not read the layout. This view uses the layout the firmware holds, not the definition file (command 0xC2).
he.noDevice: Connect a keyboard to see hall effect controls.
he.tip.selection: Settings apply to the keys you pick on the keyboard above. Click to toggle, drag across several, or use the buttons. With nothing picked, the value controls are off — pick keys first.
he.tip.press: How far the key must travel down before it registers. Turn on live depth and press a key to see where that is on the ruler.
he.tip.release: How far back up the key must come before it counts as released. Must be shallower than the press point — the firmware clamps it.
he.tip.live: Streams the real depth of the keys you picked. The bar next to the ruler follows the deepest one.
he.tip.rt: Decides by direction change rather than a fixed point. Once pressed, reversing by the release distance lets go; pressing back down by the re-press distance triggers again.
he.tip.cont: Keeps rapid trigger active over the whole travel. Without it, rapid trigger only lives below the press point and resets once the key comes back above it.
he.tip.rtRelease: How far the key must come back up from its deepest point to release. Smaller is quicker but easier to trip on a shaky finger.
he.tip.rtPress: How far the key must go back down from its shallowest point to trigger again.
he.tip.bottom: Turns the release side off near the bottom. Holding a key fully pressed, a finger still eases off by 0.1-0.3mm, and that alone would release it. Only happens with rapid trigger.
he.tip.bottomZone: How deep the protected band reaches up from the bottom.
he.tip.dead: Movement within this distance of the resting position is ignored, so vibration or tolerance cannot produce an accidental press. Leave it at zero unless the board sees vibration.
he.tip.switch: Nominal travel used to convert uncalibrated keys to mm. Once calibrated, the per-key measurement takes over. Pick your actual switch if you know it — the mm readings are wrong otherwise.
he.tip.cal: The resting baseline is tracked automatically by the firmware. What this collects is the bottom — it can only be known by pressing each key all the way down. Without it the nominal switch travel is used; with it every key is measured, so the mm values are accurate.
he.tip.fw: Pick the build output build/wish60-he.bin. If the app is running it switches to the bootloader on its own.
he.tip.boot: Switches to the bootloader without flashing. Use it to grant bootloader permission ahead of time, or to get there by hand if the app misbehaves.
he.tip.calDone: Keys painted on the board above are not calibrated yet; calibrated ones show their measured stroke in mm. The spread is how far off the nominal travel would be. Once calibration starts it flips — finished keys get painted instead.
Optional. Without it the nominal switch: Optional. Without it the nominal switch travel is used; with it each key is measured, so the mm values are accurate. Calibrated keys show their measured stroke in mm; the rest are painted on the board above.
he.tip.raw: Swaps the number under each key from mm to the raw sensor count while a key is down. Useful for checking what the sensor actually sees; the mm reading is what you normally want.
he.tip.backup: Saves everything this keyboard needs to be itself — all four profiles with their HE settings, keymaps and lighting, plus macros and QMK options. Calibration is not included; it measures this board's own switches.
he.note.backup: Calibration stays with the board — recalibrate instead of copying it. The keymap Save/Load in the keymap tab still works on its own; this file is the whole board.
he.tip.prof: Which set of settings the board is using. Everything on the screens below lives inside the selected profile. Calibration is shared — it measures the board, not your taste.
he.tip.profCopy: Copies the current profile over another number. Set one up the way you like, then copy it and change a value or two. The target's settings are lost.
he.note.prof: The board remembers which profile is active across power cycles. Calibration is shared by all four — you only bottom-out once.
Overwrite profile {{n}} with profile {{c: Overwrite profile {{n}} with profile {{cur}}? Its settings are lost.
he.tip.bkScope: All profiles saves the whole keyboard, including macros and QMK options. A single profile saves just that one — load it into any profile number to move a setup from one board to another.
he.dbg.scan: How long one pass over all 64 cells takes, and what rate that works out to. The budget is 125us (8kHz); this must stay well under it. The max time is the worst-case rate.
he.dbg.scanOver: How many passes went over 60us, out of how many. A handful out of millions is boot noise; a steady rate is a structural problem.
he.dbg.task: One pass of QMK's keyboard_task — keymap, layers, macros, lighting. Longer than the polling interval means reports arrive late.
he.dbg.taskOver: How many passes went over 125us (one 8kHz microframe), out of how many.
he.dbg.rgb: The lighting share of the task time, counted separately because it hides in the average.
he.dbg.timeout: ADC conversions that did not finish in time. Should stay at zero.
he.dbg.boot: Time spent measuring the resting baseline at power-on, and whether it finished.
he.dbg.fps: Depth frames arriving per second while live depth is on.
he.note.debug: Read straight from the board twice a second, and only while this screen is open. Counters run since power-on — unplug and replug to reset them.
he.dbg.clear: Starts the counters and maxima over from zero. Use it after changing something to see whether it helped — old records would otherwise hide the answer. The current pass time is not cleared; it is not a counter.
he.note.info: Read from the board itself, so it always matches what is actually running.
press a key with live depth on: Turn on live depth and press a key
he.tip.curve: Horizontal is actual travel, vertical is the sensor reading as a fraction. Press a key and the dot shows where you are.
he.note.curveOn: This switch uses a curve solved from the two flux figures its maker publishes. Reading it as a straight line is off by up to {{err}}mm — 1/2/3mm shims confirmed the curve is the right one.
he.note.curveOff: No flux spec for this switch, so it is read as a straight line. The middle of the stroke may be off. Picking your actual product from the list is always better.
he.note.rtBadge: On the keycap, a dot at the top right marks rapid trigger, a ring marks continuous mode. Only enabled keys are marked.
he.note.dead: The dead zone cannot go deeper than the release point ({{max}}mm). Past that it would take over the release point's job — raise the release point first if you need more.
Name: Name
Loaded — press Apply to write it: Loaded — press Apply to write it
he.flux.none: no datasheet — read as a straight line
he.note.swLinear: No flux figures, so this switch is read as a straight line over its travel. Fill both in from the datasheet to get the real curve.
he.tip.swslot: Four slots for switches that are not in the built-in table. Pick one, fill it in, then assign it to keys in SELECT.
he.tip.fluxRest: Flux at rest, from the datasheet (Gs). 0 means unknown — then the travel is read as a straight line.
he.tip.fluxBottom: Flux at full bottom-out, from the datasheet (Gs). These two points determine the whole curve.
he.tip.flux: The datasheet pair this switch was built from.
he.bootOnly: This board is sitting in its bootloader — it is not running keyboard firmware, so only flashing is available. Pick an image below and write it.
he.vendorOnly: This board is still running its original firmware, so only the firmware screen is available. Pick your keyboard below and write an image to replace it. Your current firmware is backed up first, so if the new one is broken the board restores it the next time you plug it in.
he.bootConnect.hint: If the board is stuck in its bootloader it will not show up as a keyboard. Connect to it here to flash firmware.
he.tip.fwBoard: The bootloader does not report which board it is, so pick it here. Choosing the wrong one writes another board's image.
he.note.fwPickBoard: Pick your keyboard to see its firmware releases.
he.note.fwNoBoards: No firmware releases are bundled with this app. You can still flash a file by hand below.
he.note.fwBoardMismatch: The board reports "{{device}}" but "{{picked}}" is selected. Flashing now writes another board's image.
Hold On Other Key Press and Tapping Term: Hold On Other Key Press and Tapping Term are saved per profile. NKRO applies to all profiles.
Hold two or more keys and they are re-se: Hold two or more keys and they are re-sent as if tapped. Saved per profile.
Press both of a bind and only the newest: Press both of a bind and only the newest one is sent. Saved per profile.
